note: "Agak" means "rather/somewhat/a bit" and softens adjectives; similar to "sedikit" but more common in speech.

sentences.text: Cuaca hari ini agak panas.
sentences.en: The weather today is rather hot.

sentences.text: Makanan ini agak pedas bagi saya.
sentences.en: This food is rather spicy for me.

sentences.text: Jalannya agak jauh dari sini.
sentences.en: The road is rather far from here.

note: 'Barat daya' means southwest; it combines 'barat' (west) and 'daya' (south in compass terms); used in directions and weather forecasts.

sentences.text: Angin datang dari arah barat daya hari ini.
sentences.en: The wind comes from the southwest direction today.

sentences.text: Pantai itu ada di barat daya Bali.
sentences.en: That beach is in the southwest of Bali.

note: 'Barat laut' means northwest; combine 'barat' (west) and 'laut' (sea/north in compass context) — not to be confused with 'laut' meaning 'sea' alone.

sentences.text: Angin datang dari arah barat laut.
sentences.en: The wind comes from the northwest direction.

sentences.text: Desa itu ada di barat laut Bali.
sentences.en: That village is in the northwest of Bali.

sentences.text: Kami pergi ke barat laut kota.
sentences.en: We go to the northwest of the city.

note: 'Baru-baru ini' means 'recently' and is used in everyday speech; do not confuse with 'baru' alone which means 'new' or 'just'.

sentences.text: Baru-baru ini saya pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: Recently I went to the beach.

sentences.text: Dia baru-baru ini beli sepeda baru.
sentences.en: He recently bought a new bicycle.

sentences.text: Baru-baru ini cuaca di Bali panas.
sentences.en: Recently the weather in Bali has been hot.

note: 'Camat' is a formal/official title for the head of a kecamatan (sub-district); often used with 'Pak' or 'Bu' as a respectful address.

sentences.text: Pak camat datang ke kantor hari ini.
sentences.en: The sub-district head comes to the office today.

sentences.text: Ibu camat sangat baik kepada warga.
sentences.en: The sub-district head is very kind to the residents.

sentences.text: Surat itu harus ditandatangani oleh camat.
sentences.en: That letter must be signed by the sub-district head.

note: 'Iklim' means climate (long-term weather patterns); don't confuse with 'cuaca' (daily weather); often used in phrases like 'iklim tropis' (tropical climate).

sentences.text: Indonesia memiliki iklim tropis yang panas.
sentences.en: Indonesia has a hot tropical climate.

sentences.text: Iklim di Bali sangat hangat.
sentences.en: The climate in Bali is very warm.

sentences.text: Kami belajar tentang iklim di sekolah.
sentences.en: We learn about climate at school.

note: "Jalan layang" literally means "flying road" and refers to an elevated highway or flyover bridge; commonly used in city traffic contexts, not to be confused with "jembatan" (bridge) which crosses water.

sentences.text: Mobil itu lewat di jalan layang.
sentences.en: That car passes on the flyover.

sentences.text: Jalan layang ini ada di Jakarta.
sentences.en: This flyover is in Jakarta.

sentences.text: Kita naik jalan layang sekarang.
sentences.en: We are going up the flyover now.

note: 'Kawasan' means a defined region or zone (e.g. tourist area, industrial area); more formal than 'daerah' or 'tempat', often seen on signs and in official contexts.

sentences.text: Ini adalah kawasan wisata yang terkenal.
sentences.en: This is a famous tourist area.

sentences.text: Dilarang merokok di kawasan ini.
sentences.en: Smoking is not allowed in this area.

sentences.text: Kawasan pantai itu sangat indah.
sentences.en: That beach area is very beautiful.

note: 'Kecamatan' is a formal administrative term for a sub-district, one level below a kabupaten (regency); commonly used when filling out forms or giving an address.

sentences.text: Rumah saya ada di kecamatan Ubud.
sentences.en: My house is in Ubud sub-district.

sentences.text: Kantor kecamatan ini buka setiap hari.
sentences.en: This sub-district office is open every day.

sentences.text: Kami tinggal di kecamatan yang sama.
sentences.en: We live in the same sub-district.

note: 'Makam' means a grave or tomb; not to be confused with 'makan' (to eat) — note the final 'm' vs 'n'.

sentences.text: Kami mengunjungi makam nenek hari ini.
sentences.en: We are visiting grandmother's grave today.

sentences.text: Ada bunga di depan makam itu.
sentences.en: There are flowers in front of that tomb.

sentences.text: Makam itu ada di dekat pohon besar.
sentences.en: The grave is near the big tree.

note: "Mata angin" literally means 'eye of the wind' and refers to the cardinal/compass directions (north, south, east, west); commonly used in navigation, maps, and giving directions in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Ada delapan mata angin di kompas.
sentences.en: There are eight points of the compass on a compass.

sentences.text: Guru mengajar mata angin kepada murid.
sentences.en: The teacher teaches the points of the compass to the students.

sentences.text: Saya belajar mata angin dari peta.
sentences.en: I learn the points of the compass from a map.

note: 'Monumen' is a neutral formal noun borrowed from Dutch/English; often seen in city names like 'Monumen Nasional' (Monas) in Jakarta.

sentences.text: Monumen itu sangat tinggi dan besar.
sentences.en: That monument is very tall and big.

sentences.text: Kami foto di depan monumen nasional.
sentences.en: We took a photo in front of the national monument.

sentences.text: Ada monumen baru di kota kami.
sentences.en: There is a new monument in our city.

note: 'Pahlawan' means hero or national hero; often used for historical freedom fighters (pahlawan nasional), and sometimes informally for everyday heroes; related: 'kepahlawanan' (heroism).

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah pahlawan bagi keluarga kami.
sentences.en: My father is a hero for our family.

sentences.text: Anak itu mimpi menjadi seorang pahlawan.
sentences.en: That child dreams of becoming a hero.

sentences.text: Buku ini tentang pahlawan Indonesia.
sentences.en: This book is about Indonesian heroes.

note: 'Tenggara' means 'south east' and is used in compass directions; often seen in place names like 'Sulawesi Tenggara'; not to be confused with 'selatan' (south) or 'timur' (east).

sentences.text: Bali ada di tenggara Jawa.
sentences.en: Bali is to the south east of Java.

sentences.text: Angin datang dari arah tenggara.
sentences.en: The wind comes from the south east direction.

note: "Tepi" means edge or side (e.g. of a road, river, or table); commonly paired with 'jalan' (road) or 'sungai' (river); do not confuse with 'pinggir' which is a close synonym.

sentences.text: Anak itu duduk di tepi sungai.
sentences.en: The child is sitting at the edge of the river.

sentences.text: Tolong parkir di tepi jalan.
sentences.en: Please park on the side of the road.

sentences.text: Bunga itu ada di tepi meja.
sentences.en: The flower is at the edge of the table.

note: "Timur laut" means northeast (a compass direction); don't confuse with "laut" (sea) alone or "timur" (east) alone.

sentences.text: Bali ada di timur laut Jawa.
sentences.en: Bali is to the northeast of Java.

sentences.text: Angin datang dari arah timur laut.
sentences.en: The wind comes from the northeast direction.

sentences.text: Pantai itu ada di timur laut desa.
sentences.en: That beach is to the northeast of the village.

note: 'Timur' means 'east' or 'eastern'; often seen in place names like 'Nusa Tenggara Timur'; do not confuse with 'timun' (cucumber).

sentences.text: Matahari terbit di sebelah timur.
sentences.en: The sun rises in the east.

sentences.text: Angin datang dari arah timur.
sentences.en: The wind comes from the eastern direction.

note: 'Utara' means 'north' or 'northern'; used in directions and place names; opposite is 'selatan' (south); common in addresses and navigation.

sentences.text: Rumah saya ada di utara desa.
sentences.en: My house is in the north of the village.

sentences.text: Pantai itu ada di bagian utara Bali.
sentences.en: That beach is in the northern part of Bali.

sentences.text: Angin dari utara terasa sangat dingin.
sentences.en: The wind from the north feels very cold.

note: 'Berangin' means 'windy'; formed from 'angin' (wind) + prefix 'ber-'; used to describe weather, not confused with 'angin' alone which just means 'wind'.

sentences.text: Hari ini sangat berangin di pantai.
sentences.en: Today is very windy at the beach.

sentences.text: Cuaca berangin, pakai jaket ya.
sentences.en: The weather is windy, wear a jacket.

sentences.text: Saya suka hari yang berangin.
sentences.en: I like windy days.

note: "Berawan" describes cloudy weather; related to "awan" (cloud); often paired with "cuaca" (weather), e.g. "cuaca berawan".

sentences.text: Hari ini cuaca berawan dan sejuk.
sentences.en: Today the weather is cloudy and cool.

sentences.text: Langit berawan, mungkin akan hujan.
sentences.en: The sky is cloudy, it might rain.

sentences.text: Cuaca berawan cocok untuk jalan-jalan.
sentences.en: Cloudy weather is great for walking around.

note: 'Celsius' is used in Indonesian just like in English; Indonesians always use Celsius (not Fahrenheit) for temperature.

sentences.text: Suhu hari ini tiga puluh derajat celsius.
sentences.en: The temperature today is thirty degrees Celsius.

sentences.text: Air mendidih pada seratus derajat celsius.
sentences.en: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.

sentences.text: Demamku empat puluh derajat celsius.
sentences.en: My fever is forty degrees Celsius.

note: "Derajat" means a degree of temperature; often used with numbers (e.g., 37 derajat); not to be confused with its other meaning 'degree of status/rank'.

sentences.text: Suhu hari ini tiga puluh derajat.
sentences.en: The temperature today is thirty degrees.

sentences.text: Badanku panas, tiga puluh delapan derajat.
sentences.en: My body is hot, thirty-eight degrees.

sentences.text: Air ini sangat panas, seratus derajat.
sentences.en: This water is very hot, one hundred degrees.

note: 'Hujan' means rain; commonly used in 'hujan deras' (heavy rain) and 'musim hujan' (rainy season); not to be confused with 'angin' (wind).

sentences.text: Hari ini hujan sangat deras.
sentences.en: Today the rain is very heavy.

sentences.text: Saya tidak keluar karena hujan.
sentences.en: I am not going out because of the rain.

sentences.text: Bawa payung, nanti hujan.
sentences.en: Bring an umbrella, it might rain later.

note: 'Inilah' emphasises 'this is (the one)'; more emphatic than 'ini', used to present or point out something important; related: 'itulah' (that is...), 'inilah' cannot be split.

sentences.text: Inilah rumah saya di Bali.
sentences.en: This is my house in Bali.

sentences.text: Inilah makanan favorit saya.
sentences.en: This is my favourite food.

sentences.text: Inilah teman baru saya.
sentences.en: This is my new friend.

note: 'Kering' means dry (opposite of 'basah'/wet); used for weather, clothes, food, and skin; common phrase 'musim kering' means dry season.

sentences.text: Baju saya sudah kering sekarang.
sentences.en: My clothes are already dry now.

sentences.text: Cuaca hari ini sangat kering.
sentences.en: The weather today is very dry.

sentences.text: Kulitku kering karena matahari panas.
sentences.en: My skin is dry because of the hot sun.

note: 'Lembab' means humid or moist; often used for weather or skin; don't confuse with 'basah' (wet/soaked).

sentences.text: Udara di Bali sangat lembab hari ini.
sentences.en: The air in Bali is very humid today.

sentences.text: Musim hujan membuat udara terasa lembab.
sentences.en: The rainy season makes the air feel humid.

sentences.text: Kamar ini lembab karena dekat pantai.
sentences.en: This room is humid because it is near the beach.

note: "Musim" means season or period of weather; common phrases include "musim hujan" (rainy season) and "musim kemarau" (dry season), which are very relevant in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Sekarang adalah musim hujan di Bali.
sentences.en: Now it is the rainy season in Bali.

sentences.text: Musim kemarau sangat panas di sini.
sentences.en: The dry season is very hot here.

sentences.text: Saya suka musim hujan karena sejuk.
sentences.en: I like the rainy season because it is cool.

note: 'Musim kemarau' means the dry season; its opposite is 'musim hujan' (rainy season); both are common in Indonesian weather talk.

sentences.text: Musim kemarau membuat tanah menjadi kering.
sentences.en: The dry season makes the soil dry.

sentences.text: Sekarang sedang musim kemarau di Bali.
sentences.en: It is currently the dry season in Bali.

sentences.text: Petani tidak suka musim kemarau panjang.
sentences.en: Farmers do not like a long dry season.

note: 'Musim hujan' means the rainy season (roughly October–April in Indonesia); pair it with 'musim kemarau' (dry season) to discuss weather patterns.

sentences.text: Musim hujan di Bali mulai bulan Oktober.
sentences.en: The rainy season in Bali starts in October.

sentences.text: Saya suka minum teh saat musim hujan.
sentences.en: I like drinking tea during the rainy season.

sentences.text: Bawa payung karena sekarang musim hujan.
sentences.en: Bring an umbrella because it is the rainy season now.

note: "Musim panas" means summer or dry/hot season; in Indonesia it often refers to the dry season (musim kemarau), and is commonly confused with "musim kemarau" which is more locally accurate.

sentences.text: Musim panas di Bali sangat panas.
sentences.en: Summer in Bali is very hot.

sentences.text: Saya suka musim panas karena cerah.
sentences.en: I like summer because it is sunny.

sentences.text: Anak-anak bermain di pantai saat musim panas.
sentences.en: Children play on the beach during summer.

note: 'Musim dingin' means winter; Indonesia has no winter, so it's used when talking about other countries; related words: musim panas (summer), musim hujan (rainy season).

sentences.text: Di Jepang, musim dingin sangat dingin.
sentences.en: In Japan, winter is very cold.

sentences.text: Saya suka foto musim dingin di Eropa.
sentences.en: I like winter photos in Europe.

sentences.text: Musim dingin membuat saya ingin minum cokelat.
sentences.en: Winter makes me want to drink chocolate.

note: 'Pemirsa' means 'viewers' or 'audience' and is used formally on TV; beginners may confuse it with 'penonton' (live audience/spectators).

sentences.text: Selamat malam, pemirsa setia kami.
sentences.en: Good evening, our loyal viewers.

sentences.text: Pemirsa bisa menonton acara ini gratis.
sentences.en: Viewers can watch this program for free.

sentences.text: Terima kasih, pemirsa, sudah menonton hari ini.
sentences.en: Thank you, viewers, for watching today.

note: 'Prakiraan cuaca' is the standard formal term for weather forecast, commonly heard on TV/radio; 'ramalan cuaca' is an informal synonym; both are widely understood.

sentences.text: Prakiraan cuaca hari ini hujan deras.
sentences.en: Today's weather forecast is heavy rain.

sentences.text: Saya selalu lihat prakiraan cuaca sebelum pergi.
sentences.en: I always check the weather forecast before going out.

sentences.text: Prakiraan cuaca besok cerah dan panas.
sentences.en: Tomorrow's weather forecast is sunny and hot.

note: 'Ramalan' means prediction or forecast; commonly used for weather forecasts ('ramalan cuaca') or fortune-telling; related words: 'meramal' (to predict), 'peramal' (fortune-teller).

sentences.text: Ramalan cuaca hari ini hujan.
sentences.en: The weather forecast today is rain.

sentences.text: Dia percaya ramalan bintangnya setiap hari.
sentences.en: She believes her horoscope every day.

sentences.text: Ramalan itu tidak selalu benar.
sentences.en: A prediction is not always correct.

note: 'Sekian' means 'that is all / that's it', used to formally close a speech or presentation; common in school and work settings; related: 'cukup' (enough), 'selesai' (finished).

sentences.text: Sekian presentasi saya hari ini.
sentences.en: That's all for my presentation today.

sentences.text: Baik, sekian dari saya, terima kasih.
sentences.en: Okay, that's all from me, thank you.

sentences.text: Sekian pengumuman dari sekolah kita.
sentences.en: That's all the announcement from our school.

note: "Suhu" means temperature (air, body, or water); beginners sometimes confuse it with "cuaca" (weather) — use "suhu" for specific degree readings.

sentences.text: Suhu di Bali sangat panas hari ini.
sentences.en: The temperature in Bali is very hot today.

sentences.text: Berapa suhu air di kolam renang?
sentences.en: What is the water temperature in the swimming pool?

sentences.text: Suhu badanku tinggi, aku sakit.
sentences.en: My body temperature is high, I am sick.

note: "Terang" means clear or bright (light/sun); often confused with "jelas" (clear in understanding); related: "matahari terang" (bright sun), "terang benderang" (very bright).

sentences.text: Hari ini cuaca sangat terang.
sentences.en: Today the weather is very bright.

sentences.text: Lampu di kamar ini terang sekali.
sentences.en: The light in this room is very bright.

sentences.text: Langit terang setelah hujan berhenti.
sentences.en: The sky is clear after the rain stopped.

note: 'Cerita' works as both a noun ('a story') and a verb ('to tell/share'), commonly used in casual speech; related words include 'bercerita' (to tell a story) and 'menceritakan' (to narrate something).

sentences.text: Ibu suka cerita dongeng sebelum tidur.
sentences.en: Mom likes to tell fairy tales before bed.

sentences.text: Aku mau dengar cerita kamu.
sentences.en: I want to hear your story.

sentences.text: Cerita itu sangat lucu dan menarik.
sentences.en: That story is very funny and interesting.

note: 'Minyak' means oil in general (cooking oil, fuel oil); common phrases include 'minyak goreng' (cooking oil) and 'minyak tanah' (kerosene); not to be confused with 'oli' (motor oil).

sentences.text: Ibu membeli minyak goreng di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom buys cooking oil at the market.

sentences.text: Tolong tambahkan minyak ke dalam wajan.
sentences.en: Please add oil to the pan.

sentences.text: Harga minyak naik bulan ini.
sentences.en: The price of oil went up this month.

note: "Yang di sana" means "the one over there" and is used to point out a specific item or person at a distance; beginners often confuse it with "di sini" (here) or "di situ" (there, nearby).

sentences.text: Saya mau baju yang di sana.
sentences.en: I want the shirt over there.

sentences.text: Anak yang di sana sangat lucu.
sentences.en: The child over there is very cute.

sentences.text: Ambil tas yang di sana, ya.
sentences.en: Take the bag over there, okay.

note: "Yang ini" means "this one" and is used to point out a specific item; often confused with "ini" alone, but "yang ini" emphasizes selection among options; related: "yang itu" (that one).

sentences.text: Saya mau yang ini, terima kasih.
sentences.en: I want this one, thank you.

sentences.text: Yang ini lebih murah dari yang itu.
sentences.en: This one is cheaper than that one.

sentences.text: Boleh saya coba yang ini?
sentences.en: May I try this one?

note: "Yang itu" means "that one" and is used to point out a specific thing; more natural than just "itu" alone when selecting among options.

sentences.text: Saya mau beli baju yang itu.
sentences.en: I want to buy that shirt.

sentences.text: Anjing yang itu sangat lucu.
sentences.en: That dog is very cute.

sentences.text: Tolong ambil tas yang itu.
sentences.en: Please take that bag.

note: "Yang mana" means "which one" and is used to ask someone to choose or identify something; more specific than just "mana" alone.

sentences.text: Baju yang mana yang kamu suka?
sentences.en: Which shirt do you like?

sentences.text: Yang mana tas kamu?
sentences.en: Which one is your bag?

sentences.text: Pilih yang mana, nasi atau mie?
sentences.en: Choose which one, rice or noodles?

note: 'Bertanding' means to compete in a contest or match; related to 'tanding' (match), often used in sports contexts; beginners may confuse it with 'berlomba' (to race/compete in a race).

sentences.text: Kami bertanding sepak bola hari ini.
sentences.en: We are competing in soccer today.

sentences.text: Dia bertanding di sekolah minggu lalu.
sentences.en: He competed at school last week.

sentences.text: Tim kami bertanding melawan tim mereka.
sentences.en: Our team is competing against their team.

note: 'Bodoh' means stupid/dumb and is considered rude; use carefully, as it can offend; related words include 'tolol' (even ruder) and 'pintar' (smart, the opposite).

sentences.text: Jangan bilang dia bodoh.
sentences.en: Don't call him stupid.

sentences.text: Aku merasa bodoh di kelas hari ini.
sentences.en: I felt stupid in class today.

sentences.text: Tidak ada orang yang bodoh.
sentences.en: There is no such thing as a stupid person.

note: 'Kuis' is an informal loanword from English 'quiz', used in schools and TV shows; also seen as 'kuis berhadiah' (quiz with prizes).

sentences.text: Hari ini ada kuis di kelas.
sentences.en: Today there is a quiz in class.

sentences.text: Saya belajar untuk kuis besok.
sentences.en: I am studying for the quiz tomorrow.

sentences.text: Kuis itu mudah sekali.
sentences.en: The quiz was very easy.

note: 'Lucu' means funny or cute; beginners often confuse it with 'kocak' (hilarious) or use it only for jokes, but it also describes cute animals or babies.

sentences.text: Film itu sangat lucu dan menyenangkan.
sentences.en: That movie is very funny and enjoyable.

sentences.text: Kucing kamu lucu sekali!
sentences.en: Your cat is so cute/funny!

sentences.text: Cerita itu lucu, saya tertawa.
sentences.en: That story is funny, I laughed.

note: "Maju" means to move or go forward; also used figuratively for progress; opposite is "mundur" (go back).

sentences.text: Ayo maju ke depan kelas!
sentences.en: Come forward to the front of the class!

sentences.text: Mobil itu maju perlahan di jalan.
sentences.en: That car moves forward slowly on the road.

sentences.text: Saya maju untuk membeli tiket.
sentences.en: I step forward to buy a ticket.

note: "Menjawab" is the formal verb form; the base word "jawab" is used in casual speech and imperatives (e.g., 'jawab pertanyaan ini').

sentences.text: Dia menjawab pertanyaan guru dengan benar.
sentences.en: He answers the teacher's question correctly.

sentences.text: Saya tidak bisa menjawab telepon sekarang.
sentences.en: I cannot answer the phone right now.

sentences.text: Tolong jawab pertanyaan saya.
sentences.en: Please answer my question.

note: 'Moderator' is borrowed directly from English; used in formal discussions, debates, and online forums; also called 'pemandu diskusi' in more formal Indonesian.

sentences.text: Moderator memimpin diskusi di acara itu.
sentences.en: The moderator leads the discussion at the event.

sentences.text: Dia adalah moderator yang sangat baik.
sentences.en: He is a very good moderator.

sentences.text: Moderator bertanya kepada semua peserta.
sentences.en: The moderator asks all the participants.

note: 'Paling' means 'the most' and is placed before an adjective (e.g. paling besar = the biggest); do not confuse with 'sangat' which means 'very'.

sentences.text: Ini adalah pantai paling indah di Bali.
sentences.en: This is the most beautiful beach in Bali.

sentences.text: Dia murid paling rajin di kelas.
sentences.en: She is the most diligent student in the class.

sentences.text: Nasi goreng adalah makanan paling populer di sini.
sentences.en: Fried rice is the most popular food here.

note: 'Panjang' describes length of objects or distances; don't confuse with 'tinggi' (tall/high) or 'jauh' (far away).

sentences.text: Rambut dia sangat panjang dan indah.
sentences.en: Her hair is very long and beautiful.

sentences.text: Jalan ke pantai itu panjang.
sentences.en: The road to the beach is long.

sentences.text: Ular itu panjang sekali.
sentences.en: That snake is very long.

note: 'Pendek' means short in height or length; don't confuse with 'sebentar' (short time); related: 'tinggi' (tall), 'panjang' (long)

sentences.text: Rambut adik perempuan saya sangat pendek.
sentences.en: My younger sister's hair is very short.

sentences.text: Celana pendek ini cocok untuk pantai.
sentences.en: These shorts are suitable for the beach.

sentences.text: Pohon itu pendek dan kecil.
sentences.en: That tree is short and small.

note: "Persegi" means square (shape); often extended as "persegi panjang" (rectangle); not to be confused with "kotak" (box/square informal).

sentences.text: Meja ini berbentuk persegi.
sentences.en: This table is square-shaped.

sentences.text: Gambarlah sebuah persegi di kertas.
sentences.en: Draw a square on the paper.

sentences.text: Lantai itu dipotong berbentuk persegi.
sentences.en: The floor tile is cut into a square shape.

note: 'Sabar' means patient or calm; used as an adjective or gentle command ('Be patient!'); related: 'kesabaran' (patience) as a noun.

sentences.text: Tolong sabar, bus akan datang sebentar lagi.
sentences.en: Please be patient, the bus will come soon.

sentences.text: Ibu selalu sabar mengajari anak-anaknya.
sentences.en: Mom is always patient in teaching her children.

sentences.text: Sabar ya, makanannya belum siap.
sentences.en: Be patient, the food is not ready yet.

note: 'Sederhana' means simple/modest; used for things, food, or lifestyle; related word 'mudah' means easy (not interchangeable).

sentences.text: Masakan ibu saya sangat sederhana tapi enak.
sentences.en: My mother's cooking is very simple but delicious.

sentences.text: Rumah kami kecil dan sederhana.
sentences.en: Our house is small and simple.

sentences.text: Dia suka hidup sederhana setiap hari.
sentences.en: He likes to live simply every day.

note: 'Selamat datang' means 'welcome' as a greeting to arrivals; 'selamat' alone means 'congratulations/safe', so context matters; often seen on signs.

sentences.text: Selamat datang di Bali!
sentences.en: Welcome to Bali!

sentences.text: Selamat datang di rumah kami.
sentences.en: Welcome to our home.

sentences.text: Ibu berkata selamat datang kepada tamu.
sentences.en: Mother said welcome to the guest.

note: 'Tengah' means 'middle' or 'center'; also used in 'di tengah' (in the middle of); don't confuse with 'sedang' which means 'currently doing'.

sentences.text: Buku itu ada di tengah meja.
sentences.en: The book is in the middle of the table.

sentences.text: Rumah saya di tengah kampung.
sentences.en: My house is in the middle of the village.

sentences.text: Anak itu berdiri di tengah jalan.
sentences.en: The child is standing in the middle of the road.

note: 'Tim' is an informal loanword from English; used in sports, work, and school contexts — don't confuse with 'tim' the cooking method (to steam/braise), which is less common.

sentences.text: Kami punya tim sepak bola yang bagus.
sentences.en: We have a good soccer team.

sentences.text: Tim kami menang hari ini.
sentences.en: Our team won today.

sentences.text: Dia masuk tim sekolah.
sentences.en: He joined the school team.

english: to be fetched, to be removed
note: 'Diambil' is the passive form of 'ambil' (to take/fetch); commonly used in everyday speech to mean something was taken or removed by someone.

sentences.text: Bukuku sudah diambil oleh adik.
sentences.en: My book has already been taken by my younger sibling.

sentences.text: Sampah itu diambil setiap pagi.
sentences.en: The trash is collected every morning.

sentences.text: Tasnya diambil dari meja.
sentences.en: The bag was taken from the table.

note: 'Diantar' is the passive form of 'antar' (to accompany/send off); commonly used when someone is driven or escorted somewhere, often by family.

sentences.text: Saya diantar ibu ke sekolah hari ini.
sentences.en: I am accompanied by my mom to school today.

sentences.text: Dia diantar ayah ke pasar pagi ini.
sentences.en: She is accompanied by her father to the market this morning.

sentences.text: Anak itu diantar ke rumah sakit.
sentences.en: That child is accompanied to the hospital.

note: 'Diatur' is the passive form of 'atur' (to arrange/regulate); commonly used for schedules, rules, and seating; related words: 'mengatur' (to arrange, active), 'aturan' (rule/regulation).

sentences.text: Jadwal kelas sudah diatur oleh guru.
sentences.en: The class schedule has already been arranged by the teacher.

sentences.text: Tempat duduk diatur sebelum acara mulai.
sentences.en: The seating is arranged before the event starts.

sentences.text: Semua barang di toko sudah diatur.
sentences.en: All the items in the shop have been arranged.

note: 'Dibaca' is the passive form of 'baca' (to read); very common in everyday Indonesian, often confused with 'membaca' (active: to read).

sentences.text: Buku ini harus dibaca setiap hari.
sentences.en: This book must be read every day.

sentences.text: Pesan itu sudah dibaca oleh Ibu.
sentences.en: The message has already been read by Mom.

sentences.text: Cerita ini dibaca anak-anak di sekolah.
sentences.en: This story is read by children at school.

note: 'Dibangun' is the passive form of 'membangun' (to build); used when the subject receives the action, common in everyday speech about construction.

sentences.text: Rumah itu dibangun tahun lalu.
sentences.en: That house was built last year.

sentences.text: Hotel baru dibangun di pantai.
sentences.en: A new hotel is being built at the beach.

sentences.text: Sekolah ini dibangun oleh pemerintah.
sentences.en: This school was built by the government.

note: 'Dibawa' is the passive form of 'bawa' (to carry/bring); commonly used in everyday speech, e.g. 'dibawa ke' means 'brought to'.

sentences.text: Tasnya dibawa oleh ibu ke pasar.
sentences.en: The bag is carried by mom to the market.

sentences.text: Buku itu dibawa ke sekolah setiap hari.
sentences.en: That book is brought to school every day.

sentences.text: Airnya dibawa oleh ayah.
sentences.en: The water is carried by dad.

note: "dibeli" is the passive form of "beli" (to buy); commonly confused with "membeli" (active: to buy) — use "dibeli" when the object receives the action.

sentences.text: Baju ini dibeli di pasar.
sentences.en: This shirt was bought at the market.

sentences.text: Buah itu dibeli oleh ibu.
sentences.en: That fruit was bought by mother.

sentences.text: Sepatu baru dibeli kemarin.
sentences.en: The new shoes were bought yesterday.

english: to be given to someone, to have something attached on
note: "Diberi" is the passive form of "memberi" (to give); use it when the subject receives something, e.g. "Saya diberi hadiah" — common in everyday speech, related to "diberikan" (slightly more formal).

sentences.text: Anak itu diberi permen oleh ibu.
sentences.en: That child was given candy by his mother.

sentences.text: Saya diberi buku baru hari ini.
sentences.en: I was given a new book today.

sentences.text: Dia diberi nama Budi oleh ayahnya.
sentences.en: He was given the name Budi by his father.

note: 'Diberikan' is the passive form of 'diberi' (to be given); used in formal and everyday speech; related to 'memberi' (to give) and 'hadiah' (gift).

sentences.text: Buku itu diberikan oleh guru kepada saya.
sentences.en: The book was given to me by the teacher.

sentences.text: Makanan diberikan gratis di pesta itu.
sentences.en: Food was given for free at that party.

sentences.text: Hadiah diberikan kepada anak yang menang.
sentences.en: The gift was given to the child who won.

note: 'Dibuat' is the passive form of 'membuat' (to make); used when something is made by someone, common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Kue ini dibuat oleh ibu saya.
sentences.en: This cake was made by my mother.

sentences.text: Tas itu dibuat dari kulit.
sentences.en: That bag is made from leather.

sentences.text: Nasi goreng ini dibuat dengan telur.
sentences.en: This fried rice is made with egg.

note: 'Dibuka' is the passive form of 'buka' (open); commonly used for shops, doors, or events being opened by someone.

sentences.text: Toko itu dibuka setiap pagi.
sentences.en: That shop is opened every morning.

sentences.text: Pintu kelas dibuka oleh guru.
sentences.en: The classroom door is opened by the teacher.

sentences.text: Restoran ini dibuka jam delapan.
sentences.en: This restaurant is opened at eight o'clock.

note: 'dicuci' is the passive form of 'cuci' (to wash); used when something receives the action of washing, common in everyday household talk.

sentences.text: Baju kotor itu harus dicuci sekarang.
sentences.en: Those dirty clothes must be washed now.

sentences.text: Piring di meja sudah dicuci.
sentences.en: The plates on the table have been washed.

sentences.text: Sayuran ini perlu dicuci dulu.
sentences.en: These vegetables need to be washed first.

note: 'Dikirim' is the passive form of 'kirim' (to send); used when something is sent by someone, common in everyday messages and shopping.

sentences.text: Paket itu dikirim kemarin.
sentences.en: The package was sent yesterday.

sentences.text: Pesan ini dikirim oleh ibu.
sentences.en: This message was sent by mom.

sentences.text: Barang saya sudah dikirim hari ini.
sentences.en: My item has already been sent today.

note: 'dijawab' is the passive form of 'jawab' (to answer); used when something receives an answer, often confused with 'menjawab' which is the active form.

sentences.text: Pertanyaan itu harus dijawab dengan jujur.
sentences.en: That question must be answered honestly.

sentences.text: Pesan saya belum dijawab oleh dia.
sentences.en: My message has not been answered by him yet.

sentences.text: Soal ujian itu sudah dijawab semua.
sentences.en: All the exam questions have been answered.

note: 'Dijual' is the passive form of 'jual' (to sell); commonly seen on signs and listings, often confused with 'membeli' (to buy).

sentences.text: Rumah ini dijual dengan harga murah.
sentences.en: This house is for sale at a cheap price.

sentences.text: Buah segar dijual di pasar setiap hari.
sentences.en: Fresh fruit is sold at the market every day.

sentences.text: Baju baru dijual di toko itu.
sentences.en: New clothes are sold at that shop.

note: 'Dilakukan' is the passive form of 'lakukan' (to do); used in formal and everyday speech to say something 'is done' or 'is carried out'; related words: melakukan (active), pekerjaan (work).

sentences.text: Pekerjaan ini harus dilakukan setiap hari.
sentences.en: This work must be done every day.

sentences.text: Tugas itu dilakukan oleh murid.
sentences.en: That task is done by the student.

sentences.text: Olahraga sebaiknya dilakukan pagi hari.
sentences.en: Exercise should be done in the morning.

note: 'Dimakan' is the passive form of 'makan' (to eat); use it when the focus is on the thing being eaten, common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Nasi ini sudah dimakan oleh adik.
sentences.en: This rice has already been eaten by my younger sibling.

sentences.text: Kue itu dimakan teman saya tadi.
sentences.en: That cake was eaten by my friend just now.

sentences.text: Buah segar itu dimakan setiap hari.
sentences.en: That fresh fruit is eaten every day.

note: 'dinyanyikan' is the passive form of 'menyanyi' (to sing); used when a song is sung by someone, common in formal and everyday speech.

sentences.text: Lagu itu dinyanyikan oleh anak-anak.
sentences.en: That song is sung by the children.

sentences.text: Lagu ini dinyanyikan di sekolah.
sentences.en: This song is sung at school.

sentences.text: Lagu kebangsaan dinyanyikan setiap pagi.
sentences.en: The national anthem is sung every morning.

note: 'Diperbaiki' is the passive form of 'perbaiki' (to fix/repair); commonly used in everyday speech when something needs fixing, often paired with 'harus' or 'sedang'.

sentences.text: Sepeda saya harus diperbaiki hari ini.
sentences.en: My bicycle needs to be fixed today.

sentences.text: Atap rumah sedang diperbaiki sekarang.
sentences.en: The roof of the house is being fixed now.

sentences.text: HP saya sudah diperbaiki kemarin.
sentences.en: My phone was already fixed yesterday.

note: 'Ditanam' is the passive form of 'tanam' (to plant); commonly used in everyday farming and gardening contexts in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Padi ditanam di sawah setiap tahun.
sentences.en: Rice is planted in the fields every year.

sentences.text: Bunga itu ditanam di depan rumah.
sentences.en: That flower is planted in front of the house.

sentences.text: Pohon mangga ditanam oleh petani.
sentences.en: The mango tree is planted by the farmer.

note: 'Ditulis' is the passive form of 'menulis' (to write); used when something is written by someone, common in everyday and formal contexts.

sentences.text: Nama saya ditulis di papan tulis.
sentences.en: My name is written on the blackboard.

sentences.text: Surat itu ditulis dengan tangan.
sentences.en: That letter is written by hand.

sentences.text: Resep ini ditulis oleh dokter.
sentences.en: This prescription is written by the doctor.

note: 'Ditutup' is the passive form of 'tutup' (close/closed); commonly seen on signs meaning 'closed', often confused with 'tertutup' which means 'covered' or 'shut'.

sentences.text: Toko itu ditutup pada malam hari.
sentences.en: That shop is closed at night.

sentences.text: Pintu sekolah ditutup sekarang.
sentences.en: The school door is closed now.

sentences.text: Warung makan itu ditutup hari ini.
sentences.en: That food stall is closed today.

note: 'Cangkir' means a cup (with a handle, usually for hot drinks); 'gelas' is a general drinking glass without a handle — don't mix them up.

sentences.text: Saya minum kopi dari cangkir merah.
sentences.en: I drink coffee from a red cup.

sentences.text: Cangkir ini panas sekali.
sentences.en: This cup is very hot.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli cangkir baru di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom bought a new cup at the market.

note: 'Ceret' is the everyday Javanese/Indonesian word for a kettle; often confused with 'teko' (teapot); commonly used in household and kitchen contexts.

sentences.text: Ceret di dapur itu sudah panas.
sentences.en: The kettle in the kitchen is already hot.

sentences.text: Ibu mengisi ceret dengan air bersih.
sentences.en: Mother fills the kettle with clean water.

sentences.text: Tolong taruh ceret di atas kompor.
sentences.en: Please put the kettle on the stove.

note: 'Diaduk' is the passive form of 'aduk' (to stir); used when something is being stirred by someone, common in cooking contexts; related: 'mengaduk' (active form).

sentences.text: Kopinya harus diaduk sebelum diminum.
sentences.en: The coffee must be stirred before drinking.

sentences.text: Adonan kue diaduk dengan sendok besar.
sentences.en: The cake batter is stirred with a big spoon.

sentences.text: Nasinya diaduk agar tidak lengket.
sentences.en: The rice is stirred so it doesn't stick.

note: 'diajak' is the passive form of 'mengajak' (to invite/ask someone along); commonly used in everyday speech to mean someone was invited or asked to join.

sentences.text: Saya diajak teman ke pantai.
sentences.en: I was invited by a friend to the beach.

sentences.text: Dia diajak makan bersama keluarga.
sentences.en: She was invited to eat together with the family.

sentences.text: Kami diajak bermain di taman.
sentences.en: We were invited to play at the park.

note: 'digunakan' is the passive form of 'gunakan' (to use); common in everyday speech, often interchangeable with 'dipakai'.

sentences.text: Sendok ini digunakan untuk makan nasi.
sentences.en: This spoon is used to eat rice.

sentences.text: Air ini digunakan untuk memasak sayur.
sentences.en: This water is used to cook vegetables.

sentences.text: Tas itu digunakan setiap hari oleh Budi.
sentences.en: That bag is used every day by Budi.

note: 'Diisi' is the passive form of 'isi' (to fill); used for forms, bottles, or fields that need to be filled in/out — common confusion with 'mengisi' (active form).

sentences.text: Formulir ini harus diisi dengan lengkap.
sentences.en: This form must be filled in completely.

sentences.text: Botol air itu perlu diisi lagi.
sentences.en: That water bottle needs to be filled again.

sentences.text: Kolom nama wajib diisi oleh tamu.
sentences.en: The name column must be filled in by the guest.

note: 'Dikembalikan' is the passive form of 'kembalikan' (return something); used when an object is returned by someone, often paired with 'harus' (must) or 'sudah' (already).

sentences.text: Buku ini harus dikembalikan ke perpustakaan.
sentences.en: This book must be returned to the library.

sentences.text: Uangnya sudah dikembalikan oleh toko.
sentences.en: The money has already been returned by the store.

sentences.text: Sepeda itu harus dikembalikan besok.
sentences.en: That bicycle must be returned tomorrow.

note: 'Diminum' is the passive form of 'minum' (to drink); used when something is being drunk or needs to be drunk, common in everyday and medical contexts.

sentences.text: Obat ini harus diminum setiap hari.
sentences.en: This medicine must be taken (drunk) every day.

sentences.text: Air putih sebaiknya diminum dua liter.
sentences.en: Plain water should be drunk two liters.

sentences.text: Jus jeruk itu sudah diminum adik.
sentences.en: That orange juice has already been drunk by my younger sibling.

note: 'Direbus' is the passive form of 'rebus' (to boil); used when food is being boiled by someone, e.g. 'telur direbus' (egg is boiled); common in cooking contexts.

sentences.text: Telur itu direbus selama sepuluh menit.
sentences.en: That egg is boiled for ten minutes.

sentences.text: Sayuran segar direbus oleh ibu.
sentences.en: Fresh vegetables are boiled by mother.

sentences.text: Mie direbus dalam air panas.
sentences.en: Noodles are boiled in hot water.

note: 'disimpan' is the passive form of 'simpan' (to keep/store); used when something is kept by someone, common in everyday speech about storing objects.

sentences.text: Uang itu disimpan di dalam laci.
sentences.en: The money is kept inside the drawer.

sentences.text: Buku ini disimpan di rak kamar.
sentences.en: This book is kept on the bedroom shelf.

sentences.text: Makanan segar disimpan di kulkas.
sentences.en: Fresh food is kept in the refrigerator.

english: to be told to do something
note: 'Disuruh' is the passive form of 'suruh' (to order/tell someone); commonly used in everyday speech when someone is told to do something by another person.

sentences.text: Saya disuruh ibu membeli sayur.
sentences.en: I was told by mom to buy vegetables.

sentences.text: Dia disuruh guru membaca buku.
sentences.en: He was told by the teacher to read a book.

sentences.text: Kami disuruh bapak pulang cepat.
sentences.en: We were told by dad to go home quickly.

note: 'Ditaruh' is the passive form of 'taruh' (to place/put); used in everyday speech, similar to 'diletakkan' but more informal.

sentences.text: Bukunya ditaruh di atas meja.
sentences.en: The book is placed on the table.

sentences.text: Tasnya ditaruh di dalam kamar.
sentences.en: The bag is placed inside the room.

sentences.text: Makanan itu ditaruh di kulkas.
sentences.en: That food is placed in the fridge.

note: "Garam" means salt; commonly used in cooking contexts; related words include "asin" (salty) and "merica" (pepper).

sentences.text: Tolong tambahkan garam ke dalam sup ini.
sentences.en: Please add salt to this soup.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli garam di pasar tadi pagi.
sentences.en: Mom bought salt at the market this morning.

sentences.text: Makanan ini kurang garam, rasanya hambar.
sentences.en: This food needs more salt, it tastes bland.

note: 'Gula' means sugar; common in cooking and drinks; related words: 'gula pasir' (granulated sugar), 'gula merah' (palm sugar).

sentences.text: Saya mau tambah gula di kopi saya.
sentences.en: I want to add sugar to my coffee.

sentences.text: Toko itu jual gula dan tepung.
sentences.en: That shop sells sugar and flour.

sentences.text: Minuman ini terlalu banyak gula.
sentences.en: This drink has too much sugar.

note: 'Jam tangan' literally means 'hand clock'; 'jam' alone can mean hour or clock, so context matters.

sentences.text: Saya membeli jam tangan baru kemarin.
sentences.en: I bought a new wristwatch yesterday.

sentences.text: Jam tangan dia sangat cantik.
sentences.en: Her wristwatch is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Di mana jam tangan saya?
sentences.en: Where is my wristwatch?

note: Kopi tubruk is traditional Indonesian coffee made by pouring hot water directly over coarse ground coffee; unlike filtered coffee, the grounds remain in the cup.

sentences.text: Saya minum kopi tubruk setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I drink Indonesian-style coffee every morning.

sentences.text: Di warung ini ada kopi tubruk.
sentences.en: This small café has Indonesian-style coffee.

sentences.text: Kopi tubruk ini sangat enak.
sentences.en: This Indonesian-style coffee is very delicious.

note: "Kupas" means to peel (fruit/vegetables); related: "kupas bawang" (peel onion), "dikupas" (passive: to be peeled); not to be confused with "kupas tuntas" (to thoroughly discuss).

sentences.text: Ibu kupas mangga di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom peels a mango in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Tolong kupas pisang itu untuk saya.
sentences.en: Please peel that banana for me.

sentences.text: Saya kupas jeruk setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I peel an orange every morning.

note: "Laporan" means a report or complaint; used in school, work, and police contexts; related word: "melaporkan" (to report).

sentences.text: Saya harus membuat laporan untuk sekolah.
sentences.en: I have to make a report for school.

sentences.text: Dia membaca laporan itu dengan serius.
sentences.en: He reads the report seriously.

sentences.text: Laporan ini sangat panjang.
sentences.en: This report is very long.

note: 'Merebus' is the active verb form (me- prefix); 'rebus' alone is used in compounds like 'telur rebus' (boiled egg); commonly confused with 'memasak' (to cook) which is more general.

sentences.text: Ibu merebus air di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom is boiling water in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Saya merebus telur setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I boil eggs every morning.

sentences.text: Dia merebus mie untuk makan siang.
sentences.en: She is boiling noodles for lunch.

note: "Merica" means pepper (the spice); beginners may confuse it with "paprika" or "lada", which is a synonym for pepper used in some regions.

sentences.text: Tolong tambahkan merica ke dalam sup ini.
sentences.en: Please add pepper to this soup.

sentences.text: Saya suka nasi goreng dengan banyak merica.
sentences.en: I like fried rice with a lot of pepper.

sentences.text: Ada merica di atas meja makan.
sentences.en: There is pepper on the dining table.

note: 'Panci' refers to a pot or saucepan used for cooking; commonly confused with 'wajan' (frying pan/wok), which is used for frying.

sentences.text: Ibu merebus air di dalam panci.
sentences.en: Mom is boiling water in a pot.

sentences.text: Tolong cuci panci itu sekarang.
sentences.en: Please wash that pot now.

sentences.text: Panci ini digunakan untuk memasak sup.
sentences.en: This pot is used to cook soup.

note: 'Poci' is an informal/regional word for teapot, common in Javanese and Balinese daily life; the more standard Indonesian word is 'teko'.

sentences.text: Ibu menuangkan teh dari poci itu.
sentences.en: Mother pours tea from that teapot.

sentences.text: Poci ini berisi air panas.
sentences.en: This teapot contains hot water.

sentences.text: Tolong taruh poci di meja.
sentences.en: Please put the teapot on the table.

note: 'Tumbuh' means 'to grow' for plants, children, or things that develop; related words: 'pertumbuhan' (growth), 'tumbuhan' (plant/vegetation).

sentences.text: Pohon itu tumbuh di depan rumah.
sentences.en: That tree grows in front of the house.

sentences.text: Anak saya tumbuh dengan cepat.
sentences.en: My child grows quickly.

sentences.text: Bunga ini tumbuh setiap musim hujan.
sentences.en: This flower grows every rainy season.

note: "Bawang merah" (shallot) is used daily in Indonesian cooking; don't confuse with "bawang putih" (garlic) or "bawang bombay" (onion).

sentences.text: Ibu membeli bawang merah di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom buys shallots at the market.

sentences.text: Masakan ini pakai bawang merah banyak.
sentences.en: This dish uses a lot of shallots.

sentences.text: Bawang merah ada di dapur.
sentences.en: The shallots are in the kitchen.

note: Literally 'white onion'; commonly confused with 'bawang merah' (shallot/red onion); essential in Indonesian cooking.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli bawang putih di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom buys garlic at the market.

sentences.text: Saya suka masakan dengan bawang putih.
sentences.en: I like food cooked with garlic.

sentences.text: Bawang putih ada di dapur.
sentences.en: The garlic is in the kitchen.

note: 'Cabai' is the standard word for chili pepper; commonly used in cooking contexts; related words: 'pedas' (spicy), 'sambal' (chili sauce)

sentences.text: Ibu membeli cabai di pasar tadi.
sentences.en: Mom bought chili peppers at the market earlier.

sentences.text: Makanan ini pedas karena ada cabai.
sentences.en: This food is spicy because there is chili pepper.

sentences.text: Saya tidak suka cabai yang terlalu pedas.
sentences.en: I don't like chili peppers that are too spicy.

note: Mencampur is the formal verb form; campur is the root and also used informally (e.g., nasi campur = mixed rice); related: campuran (mixture).

sentences.text: Dia mencampur air dan susu.
sentences.en: She mixes water and milk.

sentences.text: Tolong campur gula ke dalam teh.
sentences.en: Please mix sugar into the tea.

sentences.text: Ibu mencampur sayuran di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom mixes vegetables in the kitchen.

note: 'Dicampur' is the passive form of 'campur' (to mix); used when something is being mixed by someone, common in cooking contexts; related words: 'campuran' (mixture), 'mencampur' (to mix, active).

sentences.text: Kopi ini dicampur dengan susu segar.
sentences.en: This coffee is mixed with fresh milk.

sentences.text: Nasi dicampur dengan sayuran dan telur.
sentences.en: The rice is mixed with vegetables and egg.

sentences.text: Jus itu dicampur air dingin oleh ibu.
sentences.en: That juice was mixed with cold water by mom.

note: "Daging kambing" means goat or lamb meat; very common in Indonesian dishes like sate and gulai; do not confuse "kambing" (goat) with "domba" (sheep).

sentences.text: Saya suka makan daging kambing bakar.
sentences.en: I like eating grilled goat meat.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli daging kambing di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom buys goat meat at the market.

sentences.text: Sate daging kambing ini sangat enak.
sentences.en: This goat meat satay is very delicious.

note: 'Mengiris' means to slice thinly (e.g., vegetables, fruit); use 'memotong' for general cutting and 'mencincang' for chopping/mincing.

sentences.text: Ibu mengiris bawang untuk masak malam ini.
sentences.en: Mom slices onions for cooking tonight.

sentences.text: Dia mengiris tomat di dapur dengan pisau.
sentences.en: She slices tomatoes in the kitchen with a knife.

sentences.text: Saya mengiris buah untuk sarapan pagi ini.
sentences.en: I slice fruit for breakfast this morning.

note: 'Kacang panjang' (long beans) is a very common vegetable in Indonesian cooking; 'kacang' alone usually means peanut or bean, so the full phrase is needed for clarity.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli kacang panjang di pasar.
sentences.en: Mother buys long beans at the market.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan kacang panjang goreng.
sentences.en: I like to eat fried long beans.

sentences.text: Kacang panjang ini sangat segar.
sentences.en: These long beans are very fresh.

note: "Kacang tanah" literally means "ground nut"; often shortened to "kacang" in casual speech, but "kacang tanah" is the precise term to avoid confusion with other nuts/beans.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan kacang tanah setiap hari.
sentences.en: I like to eat peanuts every day.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli kacang tanah di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom buys peanuts at the market.

sentences.text: Kacang tanah ini sangat enak.
sentences.en: These peanuts are very delicious.

note: "Kangkung" is a very common leafy vegetable in Indonesian cooking, often stir-fried; do not confuse with "bayam" (spinach/amaranth), which is a different vegetable.

sentences.text: Ibu memasak kangkung untuk makan malam.
sentences.en: Mom cooks water spinach for dinner.

sentences.text: Saya suka kangkung tumis dengan bawang putih.
sentences.en: I like stir-fried water spinach with garlic.

sentences.text: Di pasar ada kangkung segar.
sentences.en: At the market there is fresh water spinach.

note: 'Kerupuk' refers to crispy crackers common in Indonesian meals; often made from shrimp or fish, served as a side snack; sometimes confused with 'krupuk' (alternate spelling).

sentences.text: Saya suka makan kerupuk setiap hari.
sentences.en: I like to eat shrimp crackers every day.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli kerupuk di pasar.
sentences.en: Mom buys shrimp crackers at the market.

sentences.text: Nasi goreng ini enak dengan kerupuk.
sentences.en: This fried rice is delicious with shrimp crackers.

note: "Ketimun" is the standard Indonesian word for cucumber; also commonly called "timun" in everyday speech, especially in Bali and Java.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli ketimun di pasar pagi.
sentences.en: Mom buys cucumbers at the morning market.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan ketimun dengan sambal.
sentences.en: I like eating cucumber with sambal.

sentences.text: Ketimun ini segar dan enak.
sentences.en: This cucumber is fresh and delicious.

note: 'Ketumbar' is the everyday Indonesian word for coriander seed, commonly used as a spice in cooking; do not confuse with 'daun ketumbar' (coriander leaves).

sentences.text: Ibu membeli ketumbar di pasar pagi.
sentences.en: Mom buys coriander at the morning market.

sentences.text: Masakan ini perlu ketumbar dan garam.
sentences.en: This dish needs coriander and salt.

sentences.text: Aku tidak punya ketumbar di rumah.
sentences.en: I don't have coriander at home.

note: 'Kol' is the everyday informal word for cabbage in Indonesia; the formal word is 'kubis', but 'kol' is far more common in markets and cooking.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli kol di pasar pagi.
sentences.en: Mom buys cabbage at the morning market.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan kol goreng.
sentences.en: I like eating fried cabbage.

sentences.text: Harga kol hari ini murah.
sentences.en: The price of cabbage is cheap today.

note: 'Mentega' means butter; not to be confused with 'margarin' (margarine), which is more common in Indonesian cooking.

sentences.text: Saya pakai mentega untuk membuat roti.
sentences.en: I use butter to make bread.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli mentega di pasar tadi.
sentences.en: Mom bought butter at the market earlier.

sentences.text: Mentega ini sangat enak di roti.
sentences.en: This butter is very tasty on bread.

note: 'Mengoleskan' is the full verb form; 'oleskan' is the imperative/command form — both mean to spread or apply something onto a surface, commonly used for butter, cream, or sunscreen.

sentences.text: Dia mengoleskan mentega di atas roti.
sentences.en: She spreads butter on the bread.

sentences.text: Oleskan krim ini ke kulit kamu.
sentences.en: Apply this cream to your skin.

sentences.text: Ibu mengoleskan selai di roti bakar.
sentences.en: Mom spreads jam on the toast.

note: "Memanggang" is the active verb form; "panggang" is the base/adjective form (e.g., ayam panggang = grilled chicken); commonly used for grilling over fire or in an oven.

sentences.text: Ayah memanggang ikan di halaman rumah.
sentences.en: Dad is grilling fish in the yard.

sentences.text: Kami suka memanggang ayam setiap minggu.
sentences.en: We like to grill chicken every week.

sentences.text: Ibu memanggang jagung di atas api.
sentences.en: Mom is grilling corn over the fire.

note: 'Menyajikan' is formal/written; use 'sajikan' for commands (e.g., 'Sajikan makanan ini!'); related: 'hidangkan' (to dish out), 'menyediakan' (to provide).

sentences.text: Ibu menyajikan nasi goreng untuk keluarga.
sentences.en: Mom serves fried rice for the family.

sentences.text: Pelayan menyajikan minuman dingin kepada tamu.
sentences.en: The waiter serves cold drinks to the guests.

sentences.text: Tolong sajikan kue itu di meja.
sentences.en: Please serve that cake on the table.

note: 'Sesuai' means fitting/appropriate/in accordance with; often confused with 'cocok' (which is more informal for 'match/fit'); common in phrases like 'sesuai rencana' (according to plan).

sentences.text: Pakaian ini sesuai untuk ke pura.
sentences.en: This clothing is appropriate for going to the temple.

sentences.text: Harganya sesuai dengan kualitasnya.
sentences.en: The price is appropriate for its quality.

sentences.text: Acara berjalan sesuai rencana hari ini.
sentences.en: The event went according to plan today.

note: 'Selera' means taste or appetite; commonly used in 'selera makan' (appetite) and 'sesuai selera' (to one's taste); not to be confused with 'rasa' which means flavor or feeling.

sentences.text: Selera makan saya sangat baik hari ini.
sentences.en: My appetite is very good today.

sentences.text: Masakan ini sesuai dengan selera saya.
sentences.en: This dish suits my taste.

sentences.text: Dia tidak punya selera makan sekarang.
sentences.en: She has no appetite right now.

note: 'Menambahkan' is the formal/active form; 'tambahkan' is the imperative — both mean 'to add'; often used when adding ingredients, items, or information

sentences.text: Tolong tambahkan gula ke dalam teh saya.
sentences.en: Please add sugar to my tea.

sentences.text: Dia menambahkan garam ke dalam masakannya.
sentences.en: She adds salt to her cooking.

sentences.text: Boleh saya menambahkan nasi lagi?
sentences.en: May I add more rice?

note: 'Menaruh' is the formal/written form; 'naruh' or 'taruh' is common in casual speech; often confused with 'meletakkan' which is more formal.

sentences.text: Saya menaruh buku di atas meja.
sentences.en: I put the book on the table.

sentences.text: Dia menaruh tas di kursi.
sentences.en: She puts her bag on the chair.

sentences.text: Tolong taruh sepatu di luar.
sentences.en: Please put the shoes outside.

note: 'Terasi' is an informal/everyday word for fermented shrimp paste, a common cooking ingredient in Indonesian cuisine; often used in sambal.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli terasi di pasar pagi.
sentences.en: Mom buys shrimp paste at the morning market.

sentences.text: Sambal ini pakai terasi yang enak.
sentences.en: This sambal uses delicious shrimp paste.

sentences.text: Terasi dibuat dari udang kecil.
sentences.en: Shrimp paste is made from small shrimp.

note: 'Tomat' is the standard everyday word for tomato; used in both formal and informal speech; related words: 'sayuran' (vegetables), 'saus tomat' (tomato sauce).

sentences.text: Ibu membeli tomat di pasar pagi.
sentences.en: Mom buys tomatoes at the morning market.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan tomat segar setiap hari.
sentences.en: I like to eat fresh tomatoes every day.

sentences.text: Tomat ini berwarna merah dan segar.
sentences.en: This tomato is red and fresh.

note: "Menumis" is the formal verb form; "tumis" is used in dish names (e.g., tumis kangkung) and casual speech; common in Indonesian cooking instructions.

sentences.text: Ibu menumis bawang putih di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom is sautéing garlic in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Aku suka menumis sayuran setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I like to sauté vegetables every morning.

sentences.text: Dia menumis tempe dengan cabai merah.
sentences.en: She sautés tempeh with red chili.

note: "Akar" means root or roots; commonly used in both literal (plant roots) and figurative contexts (roots of a problem); related words: berakar (to be rooted).

sentences.text: Akar pohon itu sangat besar dan kuat.
sentences.en: The roots of that tree are very big and strong.

sentences.text: Anak itu mencabut akar dari tanah.
sentences.en: The child pulled the root out of the ground.

sentences.text: Akar tanaman ini tumbuh sangat cepat.
sentences.en: The roots of this plant grow very fast.

english: to go from place to place
note: Casual/neutral register; 'berkeliling' combines 'ber-' prefix with 'keliling' (around/circuit); related: 'jalan-jalan' (to stroll), 'keliling kota' (around the city).

sentences.text: Kami berkeliling kota Bali hari ini.
sentences.en: We are going around Bali city today.

sentences.text: Saya suka berkeliling pasar setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I like going around the market every morning.

sentences.text: Mereka berkeliling pulau dengan sepeda.
sentences.en: They go around the island by bicycle.

note: 'Bungkus' means a packet or wrapper; used as a counter word for packaged items (e.g. mie instan, rokok); also means 'wrap it up / take away' in food contexts.

sentences.text: Saya beli dua bungkus mie instan.
sentences.en: I buy two packets of instant noodles.

sentences.text: Ada tiga bungkus kopi di meja.
sentences.en: There are three packets of coffee on the table.

note: 'Bungkusan' means a wrapped package or parcel; more informal than 'paket', often used for hand-carried wrapped items.

sentences.text: Ada bungkusan di meja dapur.
sentences.en: There is a package on the kitchen table.

sentences.text: Ibu membawa bungkusan dari pasar.
sentences.en: Mom is bringing a package from the market.

sentences.text: Bungkusan itu untuk adik saya.
sentences.en: That package is for my younger sibling.

note: 'Daun' means both 'a leaf' and 'leaves' (no plural form); also used in compound words like 'daun bawang' (spring onion) and 'daun pisang' (banana leaf).

sentences.text: Daun itu berwarna hijau dan indah.
sentences.en: That leaf is green and beautiful.

sentences.text: Saya menyapu daun di halaman rumah.
sentences.en: I am sweeping leaves in the yard.

sentences.text: Pohon ini punya banyak daun besar.
sentences.en: This tree has many big leaves.

note: 'Demam' means fever; commonly used in everyday health contexts; related words include 'sakit' (sick) and 'panas' (hot/warm).

sentences.text: Anak saya sakit demam sejak kemarin.
sentences.en: My child has been sick with a fever since yesterday.

sentences.text: Saya minum obat karena demam.
sentences.en: I took medicine because of a fever.

sentences.text: Dia istirahat di rumah karena demam.
sentences.en: She is resting at home because of a fever.

note: 'Gemuk' means fat/chubby and is fairly neutral in Indonesian; often confused with 'besar' (big); related words: 'kurus' (thin), 'montok' (plump).

sentences.text: Kucing saya sangat gemuk dan lucu.
sentences.en: My cat is very fat and cute.

sentences.text: Dia menjadi gemuk karena makan banyak.
sentences.en: He became fat because he eats a lot.

sentences.text: Babi itu gemuk sekali.
sentences.en: That pig is very fat.

note: Use 'menggendong' for carrying a person (esp. a baby or child) on your back or in your arms; not for carrying objects in bags or hands.

sentences.text: Ibu menggendong bayi yang lucu itu.
sentences.en: Mother is carrying the cute baby.

sentences.text: Ayah gendong adik ke kamar tidur.
sentences.en: Dad carries the younger sibling to the bedroom.

sentences.text: Nenek menggendong cucunya di pasar.
sentences.en: Grandma is carrying her grandchild at the market.

note: 'Instruksi' is a formal/neutral word for instruction or directive; beginners may also encounter 'petunjuk' (guidance) or 'arahan' (direction) in similar contexts.

sentences.text: Tolong ikuti instruksi dari guru dengan baik.
sentences.en: Please follow the instructions from the teacher carefully.

sentences.text: Instruksi ini sangat mudah dipahami.
sentences.en: This instruction is very easy to understand.

sentences.text: Dia membaca instruksi sebelum memasak nasi.
sentences.en: She reads the instructions before cooking rice.

note: 'Isi' means 'contents' or 'filling'; commonly used for bags, bottles, or food; related words: 'mengisi' (to fill), 'berisi' (containing)

sentences.text: Apa isi tas kamu?
sentences.en: What is in your bag?

sentences.text: Isi botol ini adalah air.
sentences.en: The contents of this bottle is water.

sentences.text: Saya ingin tahu isi kotak itu.
sentences.en: I want to know the contents of that box.

note: 'Jamu' refers to traditional Indonesian herbal drinks or tonics; commonly sold by street vendors; related words: 'obat' (medicine), 'herbal' (herbal).

sentences.text: Ibu minum jamu setiap pagi.
sentences.en: Mother drinks herbal tonic every morning.

sentences.text: Di pasar ada penjual jamu.
sentences.en: At the market there is a jamu seller.

sentences.text: Jamu ini baik untuk kesehatan.
sentences.en: This herbal tonic is good for health.

note: Literally 'wind enters'; used for cold/flu symptoms, not just a cold — very common in everyday Indonesian speech.

sentences.text: Saya masuk angin karena hujan tadi.
sentences.en: I caught a cold because of the rain earlier.

sentences.text: Dia masuk angin dan minum jahe.
sentences.en: She caught a cold and drank ginger.

sentences.text: Jangan masuk angin, pakai jaket ya!
sentences.en: Don't catch a cold, wear a jacket!

english: someone's face, the front part of something
note: 'Muka' means face or front; informal/colloquial, often interchangeable with 'wajah' (more formal); also used in phrases like 'di muka' (in front of).

sentences.text: Muka adik saya merah sekali hari ini.
sentences.en: My younger sibling's face is very red today.

sentences.text: Dia cuci muka sebelum makan pagi.
sentences.en: She washes her face before breakfast.

sentences.text: Rumah kami ada di muka jalan.
sentences.en: Our house is at the front of the road.

note: 'Obat' means medicine or drug; commonly used for both prescription and over-the-counter medicine; related words: 'apotek' (pharmacy), 'minum obat' (to take medicine).

sentences.text: Saya perlu minum obat setiap hari.
sentences.en: I need to take medicine every day.

sentences.text: Di mana saya bisa beli obat?
sentences.en: Where can I buy medicine?

sentences.text: Obat ini untuk sakit kepala.
sentences.en: This medicine is for headaches.

note: 'Pemakaian' is the noun form of 'pakai' (to use/wear); commonly used for usage of water, electricity, or items; do not confuse with 'penggunaan' which is more formal.

sentences.text: Pemakaian air di rumah harus hemat.
sentences.en: The use of water at home must be efficient.

sentences.text: Pemakaian sabun ini sangat mudah.
sentences.en: The use of this soap is very easy.

sentences.text: Ibu menjelaskan pemakaian obat itu.
sentences.en: Mom explained the use of that medicine.

note: 'Perut' means belly or abdomen; commonly used in everyday speech; related phrases: 'sakit perut' (stomachache), 'lapar' (hungry) often pairs with perut.

sentences.text: Perut saya lapar sekarang.
sentences.en: My belly is hungry now.

sentences.text: Dia memegang perut karena sakit.
sentences.en: She is holding her belly because it hurts.

sentences.text: Perut saya penuh setelah makan.
sentences.en: My stomach is full after eating.

note: 'Sakit kepala' literally means 'sick head'; use 'saya sakit kepala' (not 'saya punya sakit kepala') — common in everyday speech alongside related words like 'sakit perut' (stomachache).

sentences.text: Saya sakit kepala hari ini.
sentences.en: I have a headache today.

sentences.text: Dia tidak sekolah karena sakit kepala.
sentences.en: She is not going to school because she has a headache.

sentences.text: Ibu minum obat untuk sakit kepala.
sentences.en: Mom is taking medicine for a headache.

note: "Sakit perut" literally means 'stomach hurts/ache'; commonly used in everyday speech, not formal medical contexts; related: 'sakit kepala' (headache), 'sakit gigi' (toothache).

sentences.text: Saya sakit perut setelah makan pedas.
sentences.en: I have a stomach ache after eating spicy food.

sentences.text: Dia sakit perut dan tidak mau makan.
sentences.en: She has a stomach problem and doesn't want to eat.

sentences.text: Anak itu sakit perut sejak tadi pagi.
sentences.en: That child has had a stomach ache since this morning.

note: 'Sariawan' refers to a mouth ulcer or canker sore; commonly used in everyday speech, not formal medical context; often confused with 'sakit gigi' (toothache).

sentences.text: Mulutku sakit karena ada sariawan.
sentences.en: My mouth hurts because I have a mouth ulcer.

sentences.text: Aku tidak bisa makan, ada sariawan.
sentences.en: I cannot eat; I have a mouth ulcer.

sentences.text: Sariawan ini sudah tiga hari.
sentences.en: This mouth ulcer has been here for three days.

note: 'Bahagia' means happy in a deep or heartfelt sense; for casual everyday happiness 'senang' is more common; related word: 'kebahagiaan' (happiness).

sentences.text: Saya merasa bahagia hari ini.
sentences.en: I feel happy today.

sentences.text: Keluarga kami sangat bahagia bersama.
sentences.en: Our family is very happy together.

sentences.text: Dia bahagia karena liburan ke Bali.
sentences.en: She is happy because of the holiday to Bali.

note: 'Bahkan' means 'even' or 'in fact even', used to emphasize something surprising; stronger than 'juga' (also).

sentences.text: Dia bahkan tidak makan nasi hari ini.
sentences.en: He didn't even eat rice today.

sentences.text: Saya bahkan lupa nama teman saya.
sentences.en: I even forgot my friend's name.

sentences.text: Anak itu bahkan bisa bicara Inggris.
sentences.en: That child can even speak English.

note: 'Cuma-cuma' means free of charge; more formal/written than 'gratis', often seen in promotions or signs; do not confuse with 'cuma' alone which means 'only/just'

sentences.text: Minuman ini diberikan secara cuma-cuma.
sentences.en: This drink is given for free.

sentences.text: Anak-anak masuk secara cuma-cuma hari ini.
sentences.en: Children enter for free today.

note: 'Dicoba' is the passive form of 'coba' (to try); commonly used when trying on clothes or testing something, distinct from 'mencoba' which is the active form.

sentences.text: Baju ini bisa dicoba dulu.
sentences.en: This shirt can be tried on first.

sentences.text: Sepatu itu boleh dicoba sekarang.
sentences.en: Those shoes may be tried on now.

sentences.text: Bajunya dicoba di kamar pas.
sentences.en: The clothes are tried on in the fitting room.

note: 'Foto' is a common everyday word borrowed from Dutch/Portuguese; used in both formal and informal speech; related words: 'memfoto' (to take a photo), 'fotografi' (photography).

sentences.text: Saya ambil foto di pantai.
sentences.en: I take a photo at the beach.

sentences.text: Ini foto keluarga saya.
sentences.en: This is a photo of my family.

sentences.text: Boleh saya lihat foto itu?
sentences.en: May I see that photo?

note: 'Hari kerja' means a weekday/workday (Mon–Fri); contrast with 'hari libur' (holiday/day off) and 'akhir pekan' (weekend).

sentences.text: Hari ini adalah hari kerja yang sibuk.
sentences.en: Today is a busy work day.

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke kantor setiap hari kerja.
sentences.en: I go to the office every work day.

sentences.text: Besok bukan hari kerja.
sentences.en: Tomorrow is not a work day.

note: 'Jam buka' means opening hours; the opposite is 'jam tutup' (closing hours); common in shops, restaurants, and tourist sites.

sentences.text: Jam buka toko ini pukul delapan.
sentences.en: This shop's opening hours are at eight o'clock.

sentences.text: Apa jam buka restoran ini?
sentences.en: What are the opening hours of this restaurant?

sentences.text: Jam buka museum mulai pukul sembilan.
sentences.en: The museum's opening hours start at nine o'clock.

note: 'Jatuh sakit' is a common neutral phrase for falling ill; related: 'sakit' (sick/pain), 'demam' (fever); avoid confusing 'jatuh' (to fall physically) used alone.

sentences.text: Dia jatuh sakit karena hujan kemarin.
sentences.en: She fell sick because of the rain yesterday.

sentences.text: Adik saya jatuh sakit minggu lalu.
sentences.en: My younger sibling fell sick last week.

sentences.text: Saya tidak mau jatuh sakit lagi.
sentences.en: I don't want to fall sick again.

note: 'Kosmetik' is a neutral everyday word for cosmetics/makeup products; also seen as 'produk kosmetik' (cosmetic products); related: 'make-up', 'perawatan' (skincare).

sentences.text: Dia membeli kosmetik di toko itu.
sentences.en: She buys cosmetics at that shop.

sentences.text: Kosmetik ini sangat murah dan bagus.
sentences.en: These cosmetics are very cheap and good.

sentences.text: Ibu menyimpan kosmetik di dalam tas.
sentences.en: Mom keeps her cosmetics inside her bag.

note: 'Kurus' means thin or skinny and is a neutral/descriptive word; do not confuse with 'tipis' which means thin in thickness (like paper); opposite is 'gemuk' (fat/chubby).

sentences.text: Adik saya sangat kurus karena jarang makan.
sentences.en: My younger sibling is very thin because they rarely eat.

sentences.text: Kucing itu kurus sekali.
sentences.en: That cat is very skinny.

sentences.text: Dia ingin kurus sebelum liburan.
sentences.en: She wants to be thin before the holiday.

note: "Mengobati" (formal) and "obati" (imperative/informal) both mean 'to treat/heal'; often confused with "menyembuhkan" (to cure completely); related: "obat" (medicine).

sentences.text: Dokter mengobati luka di kaki saya.
sentences.en: The doctor treats the wound on my leg.

sentences.text: Ibu mengobati adik yang sakit demam.
sentences.en: Mom treats my younger sibling who has a fever.

sentences.text: Tolong obati luka ini sekarang.
sentences.en: Please treat this wound now.

note: 'mula-mula' means 'at first' and is used in everyday speech; similar to 'pertama-tama' but more casual; often used when describing a change or sequence of events

sentences.text: Mula-mula saya tidak suka nasi goreng.
sentences.en: At first I did not like fried rice.

sentences.text: Mula-mula cuaca cerah, lalu hujan.
sentences.en: At first the weather was sunny, then it rained.

sentences.text: Dia mula-mula takut naik motor.
sentences.en: He was at first afraid to ride a motorbike.

note: 'Nyonya' is a formal/polite title for a married woman (Mrs.), commonly used in formal settings or to show respect; similar to 'Ibu' but more formal.

sentences.text: Selamat pagi, Nyonya Sari.
sentences.en: Good morning, Mrs. Sari.

sentences.text: Nyonya itu guru di sekolah.
sentences.en: That Mrs. (lady) is a teacher at school.

sentences.text: Saya bertemu Nyonya Dewi di pasar.
sentences.en: I met Mrs. Dewi at the market.

note: 'Orang sakit' literally means 'sick person'; 'orang' means person/people, and 'sakit' also means pain or illness — don't confuse 'sakit' (sick/hurt) with 'sehat' (healthy).

sentences.text: Ibu merawat orang sakit di rumah.
sentences.en: Mother takes care of a sick person at home.

sentences.text: Dokter itu membantu orang sakit setiap hari.
sentences.en: That doctor helps sick people every day.

sentences.text: Orang sakit itu minum obat sekarang.
sentences.en: The sick person is taking medicine now.

note: 'Pikiran' means 'thought' or 'idea' (noun); 'berpikir' is the verb form 'to think'; not to be confused with 'ide' which also means 'idea' but is borrowed from English.

sentences.text: Saya punya pikiran yang bagus hari ini.
sentences.en: I have a good idea today.

sentences.text: Pikiran dia selalu menarik.
sentences.en: Her thoughts are always interesting.

sentences.text: Apa pikiran kamu tentang tempat itu?
sentences.en: What is your idea about that place?

note: 'Pintu masuk' literally means 'entrance door/gate'; use it for buildings, parks, or events — distinct from 'pintu keluar' (exit).

sentences.text: Pintu masuk hotel ada di sebelah kanan.
sentences.en: The hotel entrance is on the right side.

sentences.text: Tolong tunggu di pintu masuk ya.
sentences.en: Please wait at the entrance.

sentences.text: Pintu masuk pasar itu sangat ramai.
sentences.en: The market entrance is very crowded.

note: 'Produksi' is a neutral/formal loanword used in everyday speech for manufacturing or output; related words: 'memproduksi' (to produce), 'hasil produksi' (production result).

sentences.text: Pabrik ini meningkatkan produksi setiap tahun.
sentences.en: This factory increases production every year.

sentences.text: Produksi beras di Bali sangat besar.
sentences.en: Rice production in Bali is very large.

sentences.text: Mereka belajar tentang produksi kopi lokal.
sentences.en: They are learning about local coffee production.

note: 'Sabun' means soap in general; 'sabun mandi' is bath soap and 'sabun cuci' is washing/laundry soap — a common and everyday word in informal and formal speech.

sentences.text: Saya memakai sabun untuk mandi setiap hari.
sentences.en: I use soap to bathe every day.

sentences.text: Di kamar mandi ada sabun dan shampo.
sentences.en: In the bathroom there is soap and shampoo.

sentences.text: Tolong beli sabun di warung dekat sini.
sentences.en: Please buy soap at the shop nearby.

note: 'Sembuh' means recovered or cured from illness; often paired with 'sudah' (already) or 'belum' (not yet); related: 'sakit' (sick), 'sehat' (healthy)

sentences.text: Dia sudah sembuh dari sakit demam.
sentences.en: He/She has already recovered from fever.

sentences.text: Semoga kamu cepat sembuh ya!
sentences.en: I hope you get well soon!

sentences.text: Adik saya belum sembuh dari flu.
sentences.en: My younger sibling has not recovered from the flu yet.

note: 'suatu' means 'a/one' and is used before abstract or general nouns (e.g. 'suatu hari' = 'one day'); unlike 'satu' which refers to the number one, 'suatu' implies indefiniteness or generality.

sentences.text: Suatu hari saya pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: One day I went to the beach.

sentences.text: Ini adalah suatu masalah yang besar.
sentences.en: This is a big problem.

sentences.text: Suatu saat kamu akan mengerti.
sentences.en: One day you will understand.

english: a tablet (i.e. a kind of pill)
note: 'Tablet' is used in Indonesian for a pill/tablet form of medicine; not to be confused with 'tablet' meaning a digital device, though the same word is used for both — context makes it clear.

sentences.text: Dokter memberi saya dua tablet setiap hari.
sentences.en: The doctor gives me two tablets every day.

sentences.text: Minum tablet ini setelah makan.
sentences.en: Take this tablet after eating.

sentences.text: Saya beli tablet di apotek tadi.
sentences.en: I bought a tablet at the pharmacy just now.

note: 'Tangan' can mean both 'hand' and 'arm'; related words include 'jari' (finger) and 'lengan' (forearm/upper arm) for more specific use.

sentences.text: Cuci tangan sebelum makan, ya.
sentences.en: Wash your hands before eating, okay.

sentences.text: Tangan saya sakit sekarang.
sentences.en: My hand/arm hurts right now.

sentences.text: Dia memegang tas dengan tangan kanan.
sentences.en: She is holding a bag with her right hand.

note: "Tetangga" means neighbour; it is neutral/everyday register and can be used for one or several neighbours; related word: "bertetangga" (to be neighbours with someone).

sentences.text: Tetangga saya sangat baik dan ramah.
sentences.en: My neighbour is very kind and friendly.

sentences.text: Saya sering makan bersama tetangga saya.
sentences.en: I often eat together with my neighbour.

sentences.text: Tetangga kami punya anjing yang lucu.
sentences.en: Our neighbour has a cute dog.

note: 'Tradisional' means traditional/classical; used for food, dance, and customs; related: 'budaya' (culture), 'adat' (custom)

sentences.text: Tari kecak adalah tarian tradisional Bali.
sentences.en: Kecak is a traditional Balinese dance.
