sentences.text: Ibu memasak makanan tradisional untuk keluarga.
sentences.en: Mom cooks traditional food for the family.

sentences.text: Pasar ini menjual pakaian tradisional Indonesia.
sentences.en: This market sells traditional Indonesian clothes.

note: "Abu" means ash or ashes; also used in the common color "abu-abu" (gray); don't confuse with "Habu" or names.

sentences.text: Abu dari api itu masih panas.
sentences.en: The ash from the fire is still hot.

sentences.text: Baju saya warna abu-abu.
sentences.en: My shirt is gray.

sentences.text: Ada abu di atas meja.
sentences.en: There is ash on the table.

note: 'Bendera' means 'flag'; the national flag is called 'bendera merah putih' (red and white flag); not to be confused with 'tanda' (sign/mark).

sentences.text: Bendera merah putih ada di sekolah.
sentences.en: The red and white flag is at the school.

sentences.text: Anak-anak memegang bendera kecil hari ini.
sentences.en: The children are holding small flags today.

sentences.text: Saya melihat bendera di depan kantor.
sentences.en: I see a flag in front of the office.

note: 'Bernama' means 'is named/called'; it is a formal/written form — in casual speech Indonesians often say 'namanya' instead; related word: 'nama' (name).

sentences.text: Anjing saya bernama Kopi.
sentences.en: My dog is named Kopi.

sentences.text: Guru itu bernama Pak Wayan.
sentences.en: That teacher is named Pak Wayan.

sentences.text: Teman baru saya bernama Sari.
sentences.en: My new friend is named Sari.

note: 'Bersejarah' means 'historic' or 'having historical significance'; it combines 'ber-' prefix with 'sejarah' (history); commonly used to describe old buildings, places, or events.

sentences.text: Borobudur adalah tempat yang sangat bersejarah.
sentences.en: Borobudur is a very historic place.

sentences.text: Kami mengunjungi kota tua yang bersejarah.
sentences.en: We visited a historic old city.

sentences.text: Gedung ini sangat bersejarah bagi Indonesia.
sentences.en: This building is very historic for Indonesia.

note: 'Berteriak' means to shout or yell; more intense than 'berbicara keras' (speak loudly); related: 'teriakan' (a shout/scream)

sentences.text: Anak itu berteriak karena takut.
sentences.en: That child is shouting because they are scared.

sentences.text: Jangan berteriak di dalam kelas.
sentences.en: Don't shout inside the classroom.

sentences.text: Dia berteriak memanggil nama saya.
sentences.en: He yelled calling my name.

note: 'Diganti' is the passive form of 'ganti' (to replace/change); commonly used for objects like batteries, clothes, or broken things; related words: 'mengganti' (active), 'pengganti' (replacement/substitute).

sentences.text: Baterai HP saya harus diganti sekarang.
sentences.en: My phone battery needs to be replaced now.

sentences.text: Baju kotor itu perlu diganti.
sentences.en: Those dirty clothes need to be replaced.

sentences.text: Lampu rusak di kamar sudah diganti.
sentences.en: The broken light in the room has already been replaced.

note: 'Dikenal' is the passive form of 'kenal' (to know/recognise someone); often confused with 'diketahui' (to be known as a fact); related words: 'terkenal' (famous), 'kenalan' (acquaintance).

sentences.text: Bali dikenal sebagai pulau yang indah.
sentences.en: Bali is recognised as a beautiful island.

sentences.text: Dia dikenal baik di sekolah.
sentences.en: She is well recognised at school.

sentences.text: Warung ini dikenal karena nasinya enak.
sentences.en: This small restaurant is recognised for its delicious rice.

english: to be seen, to be looked at
note: "Dilihat" is the passive form of "lihat" (to see/look); commonly used in everyday speech, e.g. "bisa dilihat" (can be seen); related words: melihat (to look at), terlihat (visible).

sentences.text: Pantai ini bisa dilihat dari sini.
sentences.en: This beach can be seen from here.

sentences.text: Foto itu tidak boleh dilihat anak kecil.
sentences.en: That photo cannot be seen by small children.

sentences.text: Gunung itu dilihat setiap pagi oleh saya.
sentences.en: That mountain is looked at by me every morning.

note: 'Dinaikkan' is passive voice meaning 'to be raised/taken up'; related to 'naik' (to go up) and 'menaikkan' (to raise something).

sentences.text: Barang itu dinaikkan ke atas truk.
sentences.en: The goods were lifted up onto the truck.

sentences.text: Anak itu dinaikkan ke atas bahu ayah.
sentences.en: The child was lifted up onto father's shoulders.

note: 'dikunjungi' is passive form of 'kunjungi' (to visit); used when a place receives visitors, common in formal and everyday speech.

sentences.text: Pantai ini sering dikunjungi oleh wisatawan.
sentences.en: This beach is often visited by tourists.

sentences.text: Pura itu dikunjungi banyak orang setiap hari.
sentences.en: That temple is visited by many people every day.

sentences.text: Pasar ini dikunjungi ibu-ibu setiap pagi.
sentences.en: This market is visited by mothers every morning.

note: "Diturunkan" is the passive form of "turunkan" (to lower/bring down); commonly used for prices, volumes, or objects being moved down.

sentences.text: Harga tiket diturunkan oleh pemerintah.
sentences.en: The ticket price was lowered by the government.

sentences.text: Volume musik diturunkan karena sudah malam.
sentences.en: The music volume was lowered because it was already night.

sentences.text: Barang berat itu diturunkan dari truk.
sentences.en: The heavy goods were lowered from the truck.

note: 'Filsafat' means philosophy as an academic subject; commonly used in university contexts; related word: 'filosof' (philosopher).

sentences.text: Dia belajar filsafat di universitas.
sentences.en: He studies philosophy at university.

sentences.text: Filsafat adalah pelajaran yang menarik.
sentences.en: Philosophy is an interesting subject.

sentences.text: Saya suka buku tentang filsafat.
sentences.en: I like books about philosophy.

note: 'Hindia Belanda' is a formal/historical term for the Dutch colonial name of Indonesia; often seen in history books, not everyday speech.

sentences.text: Dulu Indonesia disebut Hindia Belanda.
sentences.en: In the past, Indonesia was called the Netherlands East Indies.

sentences.text: Hindia Belanda adalah nama lama Indonesia.
sentences.en: The Netherlands East Indies is the old name of Indonesia.

note: 'Istana' means palace or royal residence; often seen in place names like Istana Negara (State Palace); not to be confused with 'rumah' (house) or 'gedung' (building).

sentences.text: Istana itu sangat besar dan indah.
sentences.en: That palace is very big and beautiful.

sentences.text: Kami melihat istana dari luar.
sentences.en: We saw the palace from outside.

sentences.text: Raja tinggal di dalam istana.
sentences.en: The king lives inside the palace.

note: "Jatuh" means to fall physically; also used in "jatuh cinta" (to fall in love); informal everyday register.

sentences.text: Anak itu jatuh di jalan.
sentences.en: That child fell on the road.

sentences.text: Buah mangga jatuh dari pohon.
sentences.en: The mango fell from the tree.

sentences.text: Hati-hati, lantainya licin dan mudah jatuh.
sentences.en: Be careful, the floor is slippery and easy to fall on.

note: "Kelihatan" means 'visible' or 'can be seen'; related to "lihat" (to see); often interchangeable with "terlihat" in casual speech.

sentences.text: Gunung itu kelihatan dari sini.
sentences.en: The mountain is visible from here.

sentences.text: Dia kelihatan senang hari ini.
sentences.en: She looks happy today.

sentences.text: Bintang tidak kelihatan malam ini.
sentences.en: The stars are not visible tonight.

note: 'Pemandu wisata' means tour guide; 'pemandu' alone can mean guide/leader, and 'wisata' means tourism — commonly heard at tourist sites in Bali and Java.

sentences.text: Pemandu wisata kami sangat ramah dan baik.
sentences.en: Our tour guide is very friendly and kind.

sentences.text: Saya ingin menjadi pemandu wisata di Bali.
sentences.en: I want to become a tour guide in Bali.

sentences.text: Pemandu wisata itu berbicara bahasa Inggris.
sentences.en: That tour guide speaks English.

note: 'Perang' means 'war'; common in news and history contexts; related words: 'berperang' (to wage war), 'pertempuran' (battle).

sentences.text: Buku itu bercerita tentang perang dunia.
sentences.en: That book tells a story about world war.

sentences.text: Perang membuat banyak orang sedih.
sentences.en: War makes many people sad.

note: 'Pohon beringin' means banyan tree; 'pohon' means tree in general, so 'pohon mangga' = mango tree; banyan trees are sacred and common in Bali temple yards.

sentences.text: Ada pohon beringin besar di sana.
sentences.en: There is a big banyan tree over there.

sentences.text: Anak-anak bermain di bawah pohon beringin.
sentences.en: The children play under the banyan tree.

note: 'Ribuan' means 'thousands of' and is used before nouns; related words: ratus (hundreds), jutaan (millions); common in markets and crowds.

sentences.text: Ada ribuan orang di pasar itu.
sentences.en: There are thousands of people at that market.

sentences.text: Ribuan turis datang ke Bali setiap tahun.
sentences.en: Thousands of tourists come to Bali every year.

sentences.text: Harganya ribuan rupiah saja.
sentences.en: The price is just thousands of rupiah.

note: "Sebuah" is used before singular nouns for objects; it is the formal/written form of "satu" as an article, similar to "a" or "an" in English.

sentences.text: Saya membeli sebuah buku di toko.
sentences.en: I bought a book at the store.

sentences.text: Ini sebuah warung yang enak.
sentences.en: This is a restaurant that is delicious.

sentences.text: Dia punya sebuah sepeda baru.
sentences.en: She has a new bicycle.

note: "Terdapat" is formal/written Indonesian for "there is/are" or "can be found"; in everyday speech, "ada" is more common, but "terdapat" appears often in signs, textbooks, and descriptions.

sentences.text: Di pantai ini terdapat banyak ikan.
sentences.en: At this beach, there are many fish.

sentences.text: Di pasar terdapat banyak buah segar.
sentences.en: At the market, there is a lot of fresh fruit.

sentences.text: Terdapat warung kecil di dekat hotel.
sentences.en: There is a small food stall near the hotel.

note: "Zaman" means a period/era in history or life; often heard in "zaman dulu" (old times) or "zaman sekarang" (nowadays); not to be confused with "waktu" (time) or "masa" (period/time).

sentences.text: Zaman dulu, orang naik kuda ke pasar.
sentences.en: In the old days, people rode horses to the market.

sentences.text: Zaman sekarang, semua orang punya ponsel.
sentences.en: Nowadays, everyone has a mobile phone.

sentences.text: Ini cerita dari zaman raja-raja dulu.
sentences.en: This is a story from the era of ancient kings.

note: 'berjuta-juta' means 'millions' and is used for very large numbers; related to 'juta' (one million); common in everyday speech to express huge quantities.

sentences.text: Berjuta-juta orang tinggal di Jakarta.
sentences.en: Millions of people live in Jakarta.

sentences.text: Ada berjuta-juta bintang di langit.
sentences.en: There are millions of stars in the sky.

sentences.text: Bali dikunjungi berjuta-juta turis setiap tahun.
sentences.en: Bali is visited by millions of tourists every year.

note: 'Puncak' means peak or summit (of a mountain) but also means 'peak' in time, e.g. peak season; related: 'gunung' (mountain), 'atas' (top/above).

sentences.text: Kami naik ke puncak gunung itu.
sentences.en: We climbed to the top of that mountain.

sentences.text: Pemandangan dari puncak sangat indah.
sentences.en: The view from the peak is very beautiful.

sentences.text: Ini adalah puncak musim hujan.
sentences.en: This is the peak of the rainy season.

note: "Pusat perbelanjaan" is the formal/standard term for a shopping centre or mall; in casual speech Indonesians often just say "mal" (mall).

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke pusat perbelanjaan hari ini.
sentences.en: I am going to the shopping centre today.

sentences.text: Pusat perbelanjaan itu sangat besar.
sentences.en: That shopping centre is very big.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli baju di pusat perbelanjaan.
sentences.en: Mum buys clothes at the shopping centre.

note: 'seluruh' means 'the entire/whole' and is used before nouns; similar to 'semua' (all) but 'seluruh' emphasizes totality of a single thing

sentences.text: Seluruh keluarga makan malam bersama.
sentences.en: The whole family eats dinner together.

sentences.text: Dia membersihkan seluruh rumah hari ini.
sentences.en: She cleans the entire house today.

sentences.text: Seluruh siswa hadir di kelas.
sentences.en: All the students are present in class.

note: 'Suasana' means the feel or atmosphere of a place/event; related to 'nuansa' (nuance) but more everyday; used for both lively and calm settings.

sentences.text: Suasana pantai ini sangat tenang dan indah.
sentences.en: The atmosphere of this beach is very calm and beautiful.

sentences.text: Saya suka suasana pasar pagi hari.
sentences.en: I like the atmosphere of the morning market.

sentences.text: Suasana restoran ini sangat nyaman.
sentences.en: The atmosphere of this restaurant is very comfortable.

english: a place to eat, food court
note: 'Tempat makan' is casual everyday speech for any eating spot; 'restoran' is more formal, while 'warung' is a small local stall.

sentences.text: Di mana ada tempat makan yang murah?
sentences.en: Where is there a cheap place to eat?

sentences.text: Tempat makan ini sangat ramai.
sentences.en: This place to eat is very crowded.

sentences.text: Saya cari tempat makan dekat hotel.
sentences.en: I am looking for a place to eat near the hotel.

note: "Yakin" means to feel sure or certain; often used in questions like "Kamu yakin?" (Are you sure?); related to "percaya" (to believe/trust) but yakin emphasizes personal certainty.

sentences.text: Kamu yakin mau pergi ke pantai?
sentences.en: Are you sure you want to go to the beach?

sentences.text: Saya yakin dia ada di rumah.
sentences.en: I am sure he is at home.

sentences.text: Kami tidak yakin tentang harganya.
sentences.en: We are not sure about the price.
